title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

review.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
review.summary: The paper introduces the Vision Transformer (ViT), which applies a standard Transformer encoder directly to sequences of linearly embedded image patches for image classification. When pre-trained on large-scale datasets (ImageNet-21k, JFT-300M), ViT matches or exceeds state-of-the-art convolutional networks on multiple benchmarks while requiring substantially less pre-training compute. The authors conduct extensive scaling studies, attention analyses, and ablations, showing that ViT's performance improves with scale and that its self-attention learns global integration early. They also explore hybrid CNN-Transformer models and self-supervised pre-training, though the latter still lags behind supervised pre-training.

strengths.point: Clear and minimal method: the image is split into fixed-size patches, linearly embedded, combined with learnable 1D position embeddings, and processed by a standard Transformer encoder with a class token for classification.
strengths.quote: We split an image into fixed-size patches, linearly embed each of them, add position embeddings, and feed the resulting sequence of vectors to a standard Transformer encoder.

strengths.point: Strong empirical results on multiple benchmarks, with the best model reaching 88.55% on ImageNet, 90.72% on ImageNet-ReaL, 94.55% on CIFAR-100, and 77.63% on the VTAB suite.
strengths.quote: the best model reaches the accuracy of $88.55\%$ on \imagenet, $90.72\%$ on \imagenet-ReaL, $94.55\%$ on CIFAR-100, and $77.63\%$ on the VTAB suite of 19 tasks.

strengths.point: Demonstrates favorable performance/compute trade-off: ViT uses 2-4x less pre-training compute than ResNets to achieve the same transfer performance across five datasets.
strengths.quote: ViTs dominate ResNets on the performance/compute trade-off. ViT uses approximately $2-4\times$ less compute to attain the same performance (average over 5 datasets).

strengths.point: Open-source release of fine-tuning code and pre-trained models enables reproducibility and further research.
strengths.quote: Fine-tuning code and pre-trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/google-research/vision_transformer}

strengths.point: Insightful attention analysis showing that some heads attend globally even in low layers, and that attention distance increases with depth, confirming effective use of global self-attention.
strengths.quote: Self-attention allows \oursabbrv to integrate information across the entire image even in the lowest layers... some heads attend to most of the image already in the lowest layers, showing that the ability to integrate information globally is indeed used by the model.

concerns.point: The claim that ViT 'approaches or beats state of the art' when pre-trained on the public ImageNet-21k dataset is not supported by the reported numbers: on ImageNet, ViT-L/16 achieves 85.30% vs BiT-L's 87.54%.
concerns.quote: When pre-trained on the public ImageNet-21k dataset or the in-house JFT-300M dataset, \oursabbrv{} approaches or beats state of the art on multiple image recognition benchmarks.
concerns.suggestion: Clarify that on the public ImageNet-21k dataset ViT still trails the best CNN (BiT) on ImageNet, and reserve the 'beats state of the art' claim for the JFT-300M pre-training results.

concerns.point: The scaling study uses few-shot linear accuracy instead of full fine-tuning accuracy to save compute, but the correlation between few-shot and fine-tuned performance across model sizes is not established.
concerns.quote: To save compute, we report few-shot linear accuracy instead of full fine-tuning accuracy.
concerns.suggestion: Report at least a subset of fully fine-tuned results for the scaling study to validate that the compute-performance trends hold for the final metric.

concerns.point: The self-supervised pre-training experiment only improves ViT-B/16 by 2% over training from scratch, leaving a 4% gap to supervised pre-training, and no contrastive methods are explored.
concerns.quote: With self-supervised pre-training, our smaller \oursabbrv-B/16 model achieves 79.9\% accuracy on \imagenet{}, a significant improvement of 2\% to training from scratch, but still 4\% behind supervised pre-training.
concerns.suggestion: Acknowledge the large gap more prominently and discuss why masked patch prediction underperforms relative to NLP-style masked language modeling.

concerns.point: Random seeds are not reported, making exact reproducibility of the training runs difficult despite averaging over three fine-tuning runs.
concerns.quote: We report mean and standard deviation of the accuracies, averaged over three fine-tuning runs.
concerns.suggestion: Include the random seeds used for each run in the appendix or code release.

concerns.point: The paper uses Adam for ResNet pre-training (unconventional) and only compares Adam vs SGD for ResNets, not for ViT; it is unclear if ViT also benefits from Adam over SGD.
concerns.quote: Adam pre-training outperforms SGD pre-training on most datasets and on average. This justifies the choice of Adam as the optimizer used to pre-train ResNets on JFT.
concerns.suggestion: Report whether ViT pre-training was also compared with SGD, or at least state that Adam was used for ViT based on prior NLP practice.

questions: How well does the few-shot linear accuracy correlate with full fine-tuning accuracy across the model sizes in the scaling study? Would the compute-performance trade-off change if all models were fully fine-tuned?
The paper uses Adam for both ViT and ResNet pre-training. Was SGD ever tried for ViT pre-training, and if not, why was Adam chosen for ViT beyond following NLP practice?

The positional embedding ablation shows little difference between 1D and 2D embeddings at the ViT-B/16 scale. Were 2D positional embeddings tested at larger scales (e.g., ViT-H/14) where the grid is finer?
The JFT-300M dataset is critical for the best results but is not public. Are there plans to release it or a representative subset to enable full reproducibility?

related.title: Self-attention as the backbone: A survey on Vision Transformers
related.note: This survey paper reviews Vision Transformers, positioning the ViT architecture as the foundational work that propelled self-attention as a scalable backbone for computer vision.

related.assessment: The search results confirm the paper's foundational status: one result directly builds on the ViT-B/16 architecture for billion-scale pretraining, while the other is a survey citing ViT as the catalyst for the vision transformer paradigm. The snippets do not reveal direct methodological predecessors or concurrent alternative pure-transformer approaches, so the novelty of applying a standard NLP Transformer directly to image patches cannot be fully judged from these results alone.
